title: Adaptive Rollout Playbook Compiler for Cross-Mode Deployments
creator: Mariano Vega
description: Build an "adaptive rollout playbook compiler" that ingests a declarative rollout spec (canary percentages, AB variant definitions, shadow routing, rollback triggers) and produces environment-aware executable deployment plans for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. The compiler should validate config parity where possible and synthesize environment-specific constraints (eg. no external telemetry callbacks in Private, capacity floor checks for Dedicated, region affinity rules for Hosted). The output is a set of artifacts: a sealed rollout plan (machine-readable), console UI knobs (for percent sliders and gates), a deployment manifest for the serving runtime, and a rollback simulation report.
acceptance_criteria: Compiler accepts a declarative spec and emits separate executable plans for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with documented diffs
Plans include: canary schedule, AB traffic splits, shadow mirror routes, KV-cache warmup steps, and auto-rollback rules mapped to runtime metric sources
Private plans avoid any external telemetry or third-party callbacks and include local audit-log hooks per security policy
Dedicated plans include capacity-reservation checks and autoscaler hints; plans fail-fast if reservation insufficient
Console can ingest compiled plan and render deployment topology and gate conditions; toggles map back to compiled artifacts
End-to-end test demo: 5% canary for model_v2 with shadowing enabled and an auto-rollback trigger on token-loss regression runs in the staging cluster
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Drafted PRD and initial schema for the declarative spec. Decided on YAML-first authoring to align with infra teams.
2025-02-20: Spike completed for spec parsing and environment adapter prototype (node service). Proof-of-concept can generate different routes for Hosted vs Private.
2025-02-25: Integration design reviewed with Runtime and Console teams; identified three required runtime hooks: traffic-shaper API, shadow-mirror API, and metric-source connector.
2025-03-01: Implemented plan diff renderer and a small 'safety linter' that flags unsupported features in Private (eg. outbound webhooks). Running on CI with unit tests for schema validation.
2025-03-04: Began work on capacity-reservation checks; stubbed integration with Dedicated billing/commit service to validate reserved GPU counts prior to plan acceptance.
review_feedback: PM (Asha Patel): Ensure playbook includes a clear mapping between console controls and the underlying plan artifacts so non-ops engineers can safely trigger rollouts.
Security (Rafiq Noor): Private mode plans must default to 'data-plane-only' telemetry and emit an audit token; add explicit allowlist for any callback endpoints.
Runtime Lead (Sanjay Iyer): Auto-rollback must be metric-source agnostic — support latency, error-rate, and custom eval-score feeds; include debounce window config.
Console UX (Evelyn Park): Add a visual simulation step that shows expected traffic distribution over time and highlights rollback points for the user before applying.
SRE (Jordan Blake): Add a 'dry-run' mode that exercises the gating logic without mutating traffic — useful for chaos and safety tests.

Complete Dedicated capacity-reservation integration (billing/commit API) and write validator tests
Implement Private-mode safety linter (block external callbacks, require audit token) and unit tests
Add metric-source adapter layer to accept Prometheus, tracing-derived latency, and eval-score streams
Wire compiled plans into Console preview panel with simulation and 'apply' button
Create e2e demo in staging: model_v2 canary + shadow + auto-rollback on eval regression
Prepare RFC for rollout spec v1 and schedule cross-team review (Runtime, Console, Security, SRE)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: Keep spec expressive vs keep Private-mode guaranteeable. Consensus: allow feature flags that the compiler can 'elide' in Private outputs rather than reject user specs outright.
We considered making rollback rules only server-side, but chose to keep them in compiled artifacts so Console can surface them and run simulations.
Edge case: cross-mode promotion (Private -> Dedicated -> Hosted) requires explicit artifact translations to re-enable telemetry; include a 'promotion checklist' in the plan.
Simulating rollback probability under noisy metrics is hard — team will add Monte Carlo sim in a follow-up ticket if initial feedback shows too many false positives.
Plan for backward compatibility: compiled plan includes a 'v1-compat' flag that runtime honors to avoid breaking older serving nodes.
